label: end of year meetings and client reviews
overview: The End of Year meeting is the primary opportunity to move a client from historical, compliance-focused reporting into forward-looking advisory work. This domain holds the materials for running that meeting well: the standard EOY agenda, a rural variant, the Basic Targets dashboard method, and the advisor's psychological delivery scripts — each with who it suits and how to run it.

materials.name: EOY Meeting Agenda
materials.summary: The standard End of Year meeting structure — a timed, pie-chart agenda taking a client through an accounts review, their position on the 9-stage Growth Curve, a volatility analysis, and a Start/Stop/Keep action plan. Keeps the meeting on track and covers compliance and strategy together.
materials.who_when: General commercial business clients attending their standard End of Year financial and strategic review.
steps: Set the agenda — display the Agenda-Timeline pie chart so the client sees the exact flow of the meeting.
Conduct the accounts review — summarise draft accounts, highlight concerns, discuss the tax position, check loan adjustments, and agree filing timelines.
Review Growth Curve position across the 9 stages (Design through to Exit/Decline) and help the client identify where they sit.
Explore volatility using the "speed wobbles" analogy, and classify the cause as Common, Special, Seasonal, or Tampering.
Apply volatility options — brainstorm fixes across products, admin procedures, sales tactics, and working capital.
Create action steps — the client lists specific behaviours to Start, Stop, and Keep.

materials.name: Basic Targets
materials.summary: Connects the owner's personal income and leisure goals to a customised management dashboard. Educates the owner on core financial ratios and uses the 5-step Advisory staircase to verify data and select only the KPIs the owner can actually adjust, so the dashboard answers the vital monthly questions about business health.
materials.who_when: Business owners who need to link personal lifestyle goals to measurable business performance, and those needing a structured dashboard to track ongoing progress.
steps: Define expectations — the owner completes the expectations table documenting income and leisure-time goals.
Determine the development stages required to actually achieve those personal targets.
Apply management fundamentals — the 5-step process (Compilation, Assimilation, Interpretation, Application, Observation) to verify data and assign actions.
Review core ratios — for example the Current Ratio for solvency or Gross Margin for pricing — so the owner understands what the numbers measure.
Select actionable KPIs from a systems point of view (Inputs and Outputs), measuring only what the business can actually adjust.
Finalise the dashboard so the chosen KPIs let the owner answer the five key monthly questions, such as "Can we pay our bills?" and "Are we improving?".

materials.name: EOY Rural Meeting
materials.summary: An agriculture-specific version of the EOY meeting. Replaces the generic Growth Curve with the 8-tier Farmer's Growth Position and adds a 5-year Strategic Spending Plan, aligning the review with farming milestones and building rapport with rural clients.
materials.who_when: Agricultural clients — farmers, sharemilkers, and rural enterprise operators.
steps: Set the rural agenda — Accounts Review, Farmer's Growth Position, Rural Volatility, and Strategic Spending.
Review accounts — draft accounts, concerns, tax positions, and filing timelines, as for a standard business.
Assess the Farmer's Growth Position on the 8-tier chart — where they are now (e.g. Herd Manager) versus their target (e.g. Sharemilker), noting the timeframe.
Discuss rural volatility through the lens of forecasting probability, using the "speed wobbles" analogy to prevent reckless scaling.
Develop the 5-year Strategic Spending Plan — Lifestyle (e.g. a new boat), Operational (e.g. a new tractor), and Strategic (e.g. an irrigation system), each with monthly timeframes.
Finalise actions, optionally using the Start/Stop/Keep matrix to lock in behavioural changes for the coming year.

materials.name: EOY Advisor Scripts Only
materials.summary: The advisor's psychological-delivery toolkit for the EOY meeting — exact framing phrases to control the meeting, role-play directions for difficult "Mr Prickly" personalities, and instructions for deploying the global (Growth Curve) and local (Volatility) attention hooks through safe third-person personas.
materials.who_when: Advisors and coaches preparing their own delivery style and psychological approach ahead of client meetings.
steps: Frame the meeting structure — bridge from the personal to the business zone ("How're you going for time today?"), assume permission ("If it's o-k with you..."), take control, then share the power.

Rehearse for 'Mr Prickly' — identify the client's persona in advance and practise tone, posture, pace, and inflection to match it (e.g. matching an angry client's energy, staying high-level with a rude one).
Deploy the global hook — position the Growth Curve, reveal it via the "Bob the Chocolate maker" persona to create safe dissociation, then connect it back to the client.
Deploy the local hook — use the "speed wobbles" analogy to introduce Volatility as the reason systems must be balanced before growth.
Pivot to solutions — move into the 'WHAT-HOW' discussion across products, admin procedures, marketing tactics, and working capital.
